column1: # Ordered regex patterns -> instrument_class. Rows of kind "define" name a fragment used as %NAME% in later rows.
# Rules are tried in file order on the instrument text (dashes normalised, case ignored) with re.search; the first
# match wins. A rule built only from lookaheads therefore tests the whole text; anchor it with ^ otherwise.
# instrument_class: qtof | orbitrap_ft | ion_trap | qqq_or_qtrap | mixed | compilation | unknown.
# instrument_strat is the class a record counts toward when measurements are stratified: the instrument that
# produced the fragmentation. A mixed record whose ions came from both instruments, or from an instrument the text
# does not identify, keeps instrument_strat = mixed and is counted in no single-instrument stratum.
# instrument_strat = activation (Orbitrap/FT hybrids with an ion trap) derives the stratum from the activation the
# record names, read from its collision field and from the activation rows below (see the README): trap CID gives
# ion_trap, HCD or beam-type CID gives orbitrap_ft, IRMPD or SORI-CID in the FT cell gives orbitrap_ft, both kinds
# give mixed, nothing gives mixed. energy_only_strat is the stratum when the collision field gives only a
# normalised or percentage energy without naming the activation (the trap is the default on LTQ-based hybrids).
# A bare CID or CAD (row cid) is trap CID on these hybrids unless the record names N2 as collision gas (row
# beam_gas): the linear trap uses helium, so CID with N2 is beam-type activation in the HCD cell.
# The rows in_source, in_source_strip, tandem and source_voltage give the collision regime (README): in_source when
# the collision field names in-source activation and no collision-cell or trap activation once the in-source
# phrases are removed, or names only a source voltage; otherwise the regime of the fragmenting instrument.
# unknown also covers instruments outside the five tandem classes (sector, single quadrupole, TOF without precursor
# selection); the rule name says which.
